Title: Each customer sees only their articles at their own prices
Text: Every business customer signs in and sees only the articles agreed for them, at the prices on their own price list. Prices are shown excluding VAT.
AcceptanceCriteria: A customer sees only articles on their own price list
Prices shown are the customer's own prices, excluding VAT
A customer never sees another customer's articles or prices

Title: Customers build an order from their catalogue
Text: A customer picks articles and quantities from their catalogue, sees the order total as they go and submits the order for a delivery day.
AcceptanceCriteria: Articles can be added, changed and removed with quantities
The order total updates as lines change
The order is submitted for a chosen delivery day

Title: Customers repeat a previous order in one tap
Text: The customer's last orders are listed and any of them can be copied into a new order, which can still be edited before submitting.
AcceptanceCriteria: The last order is reachable in one tap from the start screen
A copied order keeps articles and quantities that are still available
Articles no longer available are flagged before submitting

Title: Orders close at 18:00 for the next delivery day
Text: Orders placed until 18:00 are delivered on the next delivery day of the customer's route. Orders placed later go to the following delivery day of the route.
AcceptanceCriteria: Orders placed before 18:00 get the next delivery day of the route
Orders placed after 18:00 get the following delivery day of the route
The cut-off time is visible on the order screens

Title: The order desk can change orders before the cut-off
Text: Order desk staff can open a customer order, change lines or quantities and cancel it until the 18:00 cut-off, with the change recorded.
AcceptanceCriteria: Order desk staff can edit or cancel an order until 18:00
Changes after the cut-off are refused with a clear message
Each change records who made it and when

Title: Customers follow the delivery status of an order
Text: Each order shows its status as one of received, picked, on the way or delivered, so customers no longer phone the order desk.
AcceptanceCriteria: Order status is one of received, picked, on the way, delivered
The customer sees the current status on the order
Status changes show the time they happened

Title: A confirmation email goes out for every order
Text: When an order is submitted, a confirmation email is sent to the customer and to the order desk.
AcceptanceCriteria: The customer receives a confirmation email after submitting
The order desk receives the same confirmation
The email lists articles, quantities and the delivery day

Title: Orders reach the ERP as a CSV export
Text: A CSV file with all confirmed orders is exported every evening for the 18:30 ERP import, so nothing is retyped.
AcceptanceCriteria: A CSV file is produced for the 18:30 import
Every confirmed order of the day appears exactly once
Changed or cancelled orders are reflected in the file

Title: The portal works first on a phone
Text: Customers order on their phones, so every customer screen is designed for a small touch screen first.
AcceptanceCriteria: All customer screens are usable at 390 px width
Touch targets are large enough for one-handed use
No horizontal scrolling on customer screens

Title: Minimum order value of CHF 150
Text: Orders below CHF 150 are accepted with a CHF 25 delivery fee, which is shown before the customer submits.
AcceptanceCriteria: Orders of CHF 150 or more carry no delivery fee
Orders below CHF 150 add a CHF 25 delivery fee
The fee is visible before submitting

Title: Customers pick a delivery time window
Text: Customers may choose a delivery time window within the delivery day. This is assumed and still to be confirmed with Alpine Fresh.
AcceptanceCriteria: A customer can choose one window per order
Windows follow the route's available slots
